question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III) invests 80% in listed mid-cap equities across FMCG, IT, and Pharma and 20% in unlisted BFSI names. Using the composite approach illustrated in Example 8.7 (Fund Y), which of the following is the MOST appropriate benchmark construction?

answer.text: Nifty 50 TRI for 100% of the portfolio
A composite: 75% sectoral (NIFTY FMCG/IT/Pharma/Financial Services weighted) + 25% mid-cap benchmark (Nifty Midcap 150 or S&P BSE Midcap)
NIFTY Next 50 alone, because it represents the second tier of large-caps
A fixed 10 percent p.a. hurdle rate, since all Cat III AIFs use absolute-return benchmarks

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Fund Y in Example 8.7 (nearly identical profile — thematic listed + some unlisted, concentrated sectors) uses a 75% sectoral + 25% mid-cap composite benchmark. The sectoral leg captures thematic sector concentration (FMCG, IT, Pharma, Financials); the mid-cap leg captures the market-cap tilt. Single-sector or single-cap benchmarks would miss half the exposure. **The Trap:** Option A uses Nifty 50 — wrong cap segment (large-cap, not mid). Option C uses NIFTY Next 50 — still large-cap. Option D assumes every Cat III uses fixed-rate benchmarks — not true; only absolute-return market-neutral strategies do (Section 8.8). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests benchmark-construction logic from the sell-side. XIX-C / XIX-D cover composite-benchmark construction. The SEBI PPM template requires disclosure of benchmark weights for composite constructions. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a Cat III event-driven fund with thematic concentration, disclose both the composite benchmark AND the single 'fall-back' index (e.g., Nifty Midcap 150) in the PPM — LPs use the composite for strategy-level alpha, and the single index for a sanity-check cross-comparison. Dual disclosure pre-empts LP complaints of benchmark cherry-picking.
